paragraphs.en: Food waste is often discussed as a problem of individual responsibility, but it occurs throughout the food system. Farms may leave crops unharvested when prices are too low to cover collection costs. Stores may reject vegetables because their appearance does not match customer expectations. Restaurants sometimes prepare more meals than they can sell, while households forget food at the back of the refrigerator. These losses waste not only edible food but also the water, energy, labor, and transport used to produce it. Understanding the different causes is essential because no single solution works at every stage.
paragraphs.zh: 食物浪費常被當成個人責任問題，但其實發生於整個食品系統。農場可能因價格不足以支付採收成本而不採收；商店可能因蔬菜外觀不符顧客期待而拒收；餐廳準備的餐點可能超過銷量；家庭則可能忘記冰箱深處的食物。損失的不只是食物，還有生產所用的水、能源、人力與運輸。理解不同成因很重要，因為沒有一種方法能解決所有階段的問題。
paragraphs.ja: 食品ロスは個人の問題だけではなく、農場、店舗、飲食店、家庭の各段階で起きる。価格、外見、需要予測、保管など原因は異なる。食品だけでなく、生産に使った水やエネルギー、労働も無駄になるため、段階ごとの対策が必要だ。

paragraphs.en: One challenge is that demand is uncertain. A supermarket needs enough fresh products to satisfy customers who arrive late in the day. If shelves are empty too early, shoppers may go elsewhere. Yet displaying large quantities of short-lived food increases the risk that some items will remain unsold. Better forecasting can help, but weather, local events, and changing preferences make perfect prediction impossible. Retailers can reduce waste by adjusting orders, offering smaller quantities, and discounting products before they expire. These measures require balancing convenience, availability, and the cost of unsold stock.
paragraphs.zh: 需求不確定是一項挑戰。超市必須讓傍晚來的顧客也能買到新鮮商品；若太早售罄，顧客可能轉往別家。但大量陳列保存期短的食物又增加賣不完的風險。預測有幫助，天氣、活動與偏好變化卻讓完美預測不可能。零售商可調整訂貨、提供小份量、在到期前折價，以平衡便利、供貨與剩餘庫存成本。
paragraphs.ja: 需要の予測は難しい。スーパーは遅い時間の客にも商品を用意したいが、鮮度の短い食品を大量に並べれば売れ残りが増える。発注調整、小容量商品、期限前の値引きなどを組み合わせる必要がある。

paragraphs.en: Date labels can also confuse consumers. In many markets, some labels describe expected quality rather than an exact moment when food becomes unsafe. Other dates relate more directly to safety and should be treated differently. Because rules and terminology vary by product and country, shoppers should follow local guidance rather than assuming that every date has the same meaning. Proper storage matters as well. Keeping chilled food at appropriate temperatures and using older ingredients first can prevent avoidable spoilage. Food safety must remain the priority; reducing waste should never mean eating food that may be dangerous.
paragraphs.zh: 日期標示也可能使消費者困惑。在許多市場，有些日期表示預期品質，而非食物在某個精確時刻突然不安全；另一些日期則與安全更直接相關。各地規則與用語不同，購物者應遵循當地指引，不要假設所有日期意義相同。適當冷藏、先使用較舊食材也能減少腐敗。但食品安全永遠優先，減少浪費不應意味食用可能危險的食物。
paragraphs.ja: 期限表示にも違いがある。品質の目安と安全に関わる期限は同じではない。国や食品によって規則が異なるため、地域の案内に従う必要がある。適切な温度で保管し、古い食材から使うことも重要だが、安全を犠牲にしてはいけない。

paragraphs.en: Households can make meaningful changes without adopting complicated systems. Planning a few meals before shopping helps people buy realistic quantities. Checking existing ingredients prevents accidental duplicates. Freezing suitable leftovers provides flexibility when plans change. It is also useful to distinguish between food that must be used soon and ingredients that can be stored for longer. However, strict plans can backfire if they ignore real life. A practical routine should leave room for unexpected invitations, overtime work, or changes in appetite. The goal is not perfect control but fewer forgotten purchases.
paragraphs.zh: 家庭不必採用複雜系統也能改善。購物前規劃幾餐，有助購買合理數量；確認現有食材可避免重複購買；適當冷凍剩菜能因應計畫改變。區分需要盡快使用與可長期保存的食材也有幫助。但若嚴格計畫忽略生活變動，反而可能適得其反。實用習慣應容許臨時邀約、加班或食慾變化。目標不是完美控制，而是減少被遺忘的購買。
paragraphs.ja: 家庭では買い物前の献立計画、在庫確認、適切な冷凍が役立つ。ただし急な予定変更もあるため、厳密すぎる計画は逆効果になり得る。完璧な管理より、買ったものを忘れない習慣が大切だ。

paragraphs.en: Restaurants face different pressures. Customers expect a menu to remain available, but kitchens cannot know exactly which dishes will be ordered. Reviewing sales patterns and preparing ingredients in flexible portions can reduce unnecessary cooking. Staff training helps teams handle storage and preparation consistently. Some businesses donate suitable surplus food through established channels, although safety, timing, and logistics can limit what is possible. Donation is valuable, but preventing excess production in the first place usually avoids using resources unnecessarily. Waste prevention therefore belongs in everyday operational decisions, not only charitable activities.
paragraphs.zh: 餐廳面臨不同壓力。顧客希望菜單上的餐點隨時有供應，但廚房無法準確知道點餐量。分析銷售模式、以彈性份量備料可減少多餘烹調；員工訓練有助維持一致的保存與準備流程。部分企業透過既有管道捐贈適合的剩餘食品，但安全、時間與物流會限制可行性。捐贈有價值，但事先避免過量生產通常更能節省資源。減少浪費應納入日常營運決策。
paragraphs.ja: 飲食店は品切れを避けたいが注文数を正確には読めない。販売傾向の分析、柔軟な仕込み、保管方法の教育が役立つ。余剰食品の寄付には安全と物流の制約があるため、まず作りすぎない運営が重要だ。

paragraphs.en: Food waste is ultimately a coordination problem as well as an environmental one. Farmers, retailers, restaurants, governments, and households make decisions with different information and incentives. Improvements depend on identifying where losses occur and testing responses suited to those circumstances. Measuring waste consistently helps organizations learn whether a change is effective. Public awareness can encourage better habits, but it should not obscure the role of pricing, contracts, infrastructure, and business practices. A more efficient food system will emerge from many practical adjustments rather than a single dramatic solution.
paragraphs.zh: 食物浪費最終既是環境問題，也是協調問題。農民、零售商、餐廳、政府與家庭依不同資訊與誘因決策。改善取決於找出損失發生處，再測試適合當地情況的對策。一致衡量浪費有助了解改變是否有效。公眾意識可促進習慣改善，但不應忽略定價、契約、基礎設施與企業做法的影響。更有效率的食品系統來自許多實際調整，而非單一戲劇性解方。
paragraphs.ja: 食品ロスは環境問題であると同時に関係者間の調整問題でもある。農家、店舗、飲食店、行政、家庭では情報と動機が異なる。損失の場所を測定し、それぞれに合った対策を検証することが重要だ。
